finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /restore passes attacker-controlled params[:state] through Base64.decode64 into Marshal.load with no authentication, signature, or type restriction, allowing arbitrary code execution via a crafted Marshal payload.
finding.source: app.rb:5 post "/restore" -> params[:state] (HTTP form body or query string, attacker-controlled, no auth)

trace.note: Route POST /restore defined with no authentication check
params[:state] read and base64-decoded (encoding only, not a control)
Marshal.load deserializes attacker bytes; gadget chains execute during load
state.inspect runs only after the load has already executed any payload

finding.guards_checked: No route auth; no HMAC/signature on serialized data; no class allowlist; Base64.decode64 is not a security control. Also checked /import (app.rb:10-13): JSON.parse default does not instantiate arbitrary classes, so SAFE; data.keys on non-object only yields a 500, not reportable.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.rb:5 defines `post "/restore"` with no auth filter, before/after block, or middleware, and the directory contains only app.rb. Line 6 decodes and calls Marshal.load with no signature check or class allowlist. Line 7 runs only after the load returns. The /import route (app.rb:10-13) is not a guard for this sink.
verdict.reason: Anonymous POST to /restore at app.rb:5 reaches Marshal.load(Base64.decode64(params[:state])) at app.rb:6 with no effective control in between, and Marshal.load on attacker-supplied bytes is a known code-execution sink, so the finding stands. The one caveat is that a working gadget chain depends on which classes are loaded, so the "arbitrary code execution" wording is the standard assumption for untrusted Marshal rather than something this file proves on its own.
